title: Parallel Committed-Boundary Restart Composition Architecture Audit

invariants.note: No alternate SWAP kernel or use-case-specific kernel is introduced; composition reuses the admitted shared runtime/kernel.
Restart remains serialization-neutral and kernel/source code receives no file, path, parser or format dependency.
Immutable parameters, forcing, committed state, numerical configuration and returned results remain separate objects across destroy/reconstruct/restore/continue.
Restart records persist only committed continuation state plus stable identity/provenance; no unused option state or immutable parameter payload is duplicated.
Worker backends and transaction controls are allocated after parallel admission on each continuation invocation; worker/Newton/Jacobian/warm-start scratch is absent from restart records.
Existing canonical scheduling and worker-pool storage remain unchanged; no per-column heavy solver object is added.
Only committed-boundary state is exported; restore is whole-registry atomic via candidate registry publication before parallel continuation.
Destroy/reconstruct/restore followed by parallel continuation reproduces uninterrupted committed endpoints; no trial state is promoted to physical authority.
Composition uses generic non-calendar t0, midpoint and t1 intervals; no day/month/year or midnight assumption is introduced.
No coupling-window policy is changed; committed-boundary restart remains compatible with generic [t0,t1] windows.
Checkpoint/commit provenance and rollback-safe restart publication are exercised before parallel execution; coupling transaction semantics are not weakened.
Groundwater head/flux interface semantics are untouched by this composition-only workunit.
Per-column residual <= 1e-12 cm is a hard gate and aggregate authoritative mass accounting must remain complete/identical after restart continuation.
Interface response sensitivities and tangent production are untouched.
Restart composition does not add predictor/corrector physical solves or alter coupling-cost policy.
Irregular batches through 32 columns and 2/4 workers are exercised without per-column heavy solver persistence; this is a bounded qualification sample, not a scale-performance claim.
No MODFLOW-cell-to-tile ownership or area-fraction mapping is introduced into SWAP.
Deep-vadose remains an external optional component and is outside this frozen profile.
No component transition storage or deep-vadose/direct-coupling handoff is modified.
The existing soil-water solver contract and admitted reference Richards implementation are reused unchanged; no solver lock-in is added.
Existing physical process implementations are reused; restart and parallel orchestration do not duplicate SWAP physics.
No module is coupled to HeadCalc internal arrays by F-MR32.
The frozen physical profile remains exactly the admitted F-CI30 profile; numerical worker count/order changes do not silently alter physics.
No solver fallback ladder, tolerance, retry policy or bounded-cost policy is modified.
Reference/serialized execution remains available and is explicitly used as one restart-origin oracle; no reference mode is removed.
Existing per-column and aggregate diagnostics, transaction revisions, mass fields and runtime diagnostics are compared across uninterrupted and restarted continuations.
Optional restart functionality persists no worker scratch and adds no per-column runtime allocation beyond the admitted compact committed record.
Runtime composes reconstructed registry identity, restart restore and parallel worker execution; SWAP physics remains unaware of external system composition.
Current-canonical composition is source-pinned and uses generic times; no .swp, path, midnight, daily-step or mandatory MODFLOW dependency is assumed.
F-MR32 has an explicit source lock, frozen attack matrix, fail-closed runner, owner CI and this 30-invariant audit.
